translations.text: A king must rule a kingdom. Cities can be seen from far away, the skilful work of giants, those that are on this earth, the wondrous work of wall-stones.
Wind is the swiftest thing in the air; thunder is at times the loudest. The glories of Christ are great; fate is strongest.

Winter is coldest, spring frostiest (it stays cold longest), summer brightest with sunshine (the sun is hottest then), autumn most gloriously blessed: it brings to men the year's fruits, which God sends them.
Truth is most evident; treasure is most precious, gold, to every man; and an old man is wisest, made wise by the years gone by, he who has lived through much before.
Wax is wondrously sticky. Clouds glide.
Good companions must urge a young prince on to battle and to the giving of rings.
Cattle must breed and bear young on the earth. A star must shine brightly in the heavens, as the Creator commanded it.
